summary: Breakwater light off Ashland, Wisconsin, first exhibited 15 October 1915; keepers lived ashore until automation, which sources date from 1961 to 1980.

lens.where: Fresnel lens sent to a Coast Guard station for survey; present whereabouts unknown (NRHP)

structures.type: reinforced-concrete pyramidal tower on a concrete pier
structures.note: 58 feet per NRHP; the record's 17.0 m and the USLHS record's 55 ft differ

staffing.note: Automated 1961 (NRHP), 1962 (LighthouseFriends) or 1980 (USLHS record); the sources disagree.

access.note: Access to the lighthouse is by boat (NRHP). LighthouseFriends says the tower is closed.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard per the NRHP listing form; National Park Service (Apostle Islands National Lakeshore) per LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record, after a 2014 measure in the 2015 National Defense Authorization Act

events.note: Fixed light on a pole at the end of the breakwater, before the permanent light.
Congress appropriated funds for a permanent lighthouse; LighthouseFriends gives $25,000 on 22 October 1913.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens placed in operation on 15 October 1915 (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper R. W. Campbell helped the occupants of the disabled motorboat U 297. The Bulletin gives 28 September 1924; LighthouseFriends gives 29 September.
Submarine cable damaged; light out of service until it resumed on 15 June 1925 (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper Frank H. Mersy marooned at the tower by a storm, reached over ice by men on skis. LighthouseFriends is the only source read for this.
NRHP gives 1961; LighthouseFriends gives 1962; the USLHS record gives 1980. Sources disagree.
Lens replaced by a modern optic (LighthouseFriends). The USLHS record gives 1980 as the year it was automated.
Vandals removed the watch room's brass-framed port-lights (NRHP).
Transferred to the National Park Service by a 2014 measure in the 2015 National Defense Authorization Act (LighthouseFriends); centennial and transfer celebration 11 July 2015.

corrections.why: 1913 is the year Congress appropriated money for the light (and the USLHS 'station established' year). The beacon was first exhibited on 15 October 1915 (NRHP; Commissioner's 1916 report). The record's own 1915 first_lit event agrees with 1915.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The different first years are different events: a fixed light on a pole at the breakwater's end in 1911, the 1913 appropriation, and the lighthouse first exhibited on 15 October 1915 (NRHP; Commissioner's 1916 report).

notes_for_editor: Roster matched by name and position (0.04 km). Ownership: the NRHP text (Coast Guard owner) predates the 2015 transfer that LighthouseFriends describes (a 2014 measure in the 2015 NDAA; celebration 11 July 2015); the USLHS place record gives the National Park Service (Apostle Islands NL). The story gives both and dates each. Agency field changed to match. Automation year: NRHP 1961, LighthouseFriends 1962, USLHS record 1980; the story says the sources disagree. Lens: NRHP removed 1967, LighthouseFriends replaced 1980. Focal height: NRHP focal plane 60 ft above lake level (18.3 m), replacing the earlier record value of 18.0 m. Tower height: NRHP 58 ft; record 17.0 m; USLHS 55 ft. Range: NRHP says visible '9 miles in clear weather' with no nautical qualifier, so the record's range_nm 9.0 was removed. Characteristic: LighthouseFriends describes a 1915 sign flasher giving 2 s light and 1 s eclipse; NRHP and the record give Fl W 6s today; the story says the two do not match and does not reconcile them. The 1916 Commissioner report places the boathouse 'on shore in the city of Ashland' and also 'on a submarine site on cribwork'; the story quotes both without resolving the wording. Bulletin 1915 p. 2 tender report mentions Ashland's concrete progress in the same column as a lightship rescue elsewhere; the rescue is not Ashland's and is not used. Bulletin 1924-1929 index page numbers do not match the bound PDF pages; the PDF page is cited. Bergan's death (1922), the 1925 cable outage and the 1926 Mersy incident rest on LighthouseFriends alone; no newspaper confirmed any of these (one Chronicling America search for 1915-1916 found only an unrelated page). The Bulletin index's 'Mersy, Frank, keeper Manitou Island' is not connected to Ashland by any source read, so no other_stations entry was made. Seseman (1947-1962) is named only in his public role, with no personal detail. Coast Guard names from the roster are kept as role 'other' because the archive gives no position.
